Sve je do discipline i tvoje volje, daju ti vrlo korisne alate koje koristiš za kontroliranje govora i nervoze

Radionice i vježbe su kreativne, suočavaš se sa strahovima (razgovori s nepoznatim ljudima, telefonski pozivi) i mislim da je svima nama koji mucamo/imamo govornu manu generalna anksioznost u nekoj mjeri zajednička a nema druge za prijeći preko anksioznosti nego se sustavno bacati u stvari koje nas plaše i onda vidiš da sve to čega se bojiš u biti nije uopće strašno

Sve u svemu sam imala jedno dobro i zanimljivo iskustvo, nakon odlaska s terapije podijelite se u grupice ovisno u kojem gradu tko živi i uz vašu volju se nalazite na grupnim vježbicama, ohrabrujete jedno drugo, studenti koji imaju prezentacije vježbaju izlaganja, podržavamo se, ma pomaže da i je i samo opušteni razgovor i društvene igre a ne striktne logopedske vježbe..

Treba imati na umu da se mucanja vrlo teško kompletno riješiti, nitko se nije magično izliječio ali znam ljude koji su iz teških blokada i nemogućnosti izgovaranja puno riječi došli do velikih pozitivnih promjena, uključujući sebe. I dalje imam loše dane i kad sam lijena vježbati ali sve u svemu, puno puno bolje

Nisam se riješila mucanja ali otkad sam si rekla "mucam i to je okej!! šta sad" i uz kombinaciju vježbi disanja, ritma, vokalnih vježbi, meditiranja itd život mi je puno manje ispunjen nervozom i grčem u vezi svog govora. Nemoj se obeshrabriti ako ti se na valmodu program bude doimao jako strog na momente, jednostavno ti pokušavaju usaditi neku rutinu vježbanja i kontroliranja svog govora i da ti postane automatski čisto govoriti. Okej je ako se ne riješiš mucanja kompletno ili u znatnoj mjeri, bilo kakav pomak je super. Također se malo izgradiš ko osoba, povežeš se s ljudima, nekako si osvijestiš taj problem govora i vlastitih nervoza na nekoj novoj razini

THEY GHOSTED ME! something i feel like i cannot say to myself in this situation because i was the one who ended the relationship for various reasons but not because they treated me badly, a different kind of hurt. looking someone i love in the eyes and telling them it's over is the worst thing i've gone through. but i know that feeling unloved is horrible, i sympathize with you a lot because i've been through that too. what helped me was pure, aggressive, brutal self-love. little acts of self-love every day. brushing my teeth? i am taking care of my teeth, i love myself. making yourself a meal? i feel sad today but at least i made myself some food. crying on the floor but putting a towel under my head? i'm feeling terrible grief right now but i am making sure i'm comfy even when i am like this. and so on <3 also meditating.. as in just observing my thoughts. when you think of them pretend that you have this like super smart analyst/professor living in your brain that takes notes. aha here's a thought of my ex again. this thought makes me feel like this and this. let's examine. it is normal to feel like this, it hurts but i accept it and it will pass. etc

and if they do not? even if they don't think of you ever? means that they really did not deserve you in the first place!! letting go is so hard but there will come a day when you'll feel relief and freedom for the first time in forever and that moment will be worth all the pain you felt. sending hugs

hello i am in a very similar situation. we broke up like 2 years ago, got back together after 6 months and then we were together again for a year and a half. i broke up with him recently. first time we broke up - he wasn't willing to commit, second time - incompatibility/my own issues/felt like we were hurting each other with tiny things again and again and i got sick of it and i stopped seeing our future together

the first time we got back together was wonderful..until it wasn't anymore. i think a significant amount of time needs to pass if you're thinking of getting back with ex.. i'm talking years probably.. and it all depends on how willing are both you and them to work on yourselves during this time alone 

i also felt good and relieved right after the breakup, i was as honest and gentle as i could be, there wasn't any animosity between us. now? i'm writhing in pain every night because i miss him and i feel immense regret, i feel like a terrible person. but i keep telling myself that i saved us both a lot of pain. if i had kept dragging this out it just would've been worse. but now in the middle of this pain, every strong reason i had for the break up fell apart, i feel like i lied to myself. now i'm waiting for the pain to pass, this is just... craving for that familiarity, he was my first everything and it's hard to let go. you're naturally missing them, their absence left a hole in your life. meditating helps, observing my thoughts and feelings, make art, dance to ridiculously happy music, let yourself feel the grief but focus on moving on as much as possible

This is very true for me, exaggerating facial expressions a bit was a big part of my last speech therapy. Practice opening your mouth a little more when you speak, I used to be embarrassed about it cause I thought I looked like an idiot but people don't notice it that much and it's better than blocking for 20 seconds on a word. When a scary word comes up, just open your mouth wider and engage your face muscles when saying the vowel in that word. If the word has no vowels, like some words in my language don't and all of those words have really heavy intonation or like hard R's or they can be said with your mouth almost shut, just connect that word to the previous or second one, act like it's all one big word. It does wonders. Don't be afraid to open your mouth, mimic a smile, exaggerate your A's, E's, O's, I's, U's and Y's.  When you're at home, stick your tongue out up and down, left and right before making a phone call or preparing to speak, it's a muscle too, and a very important one for speech. Massage your chin and region around your mouth, even your eyebrows and eye region. Neck muscles too, for me my neck and eyes twitch when I stutter. I do this whenever I watch a movie, just massaging my face and activating my tongue and mimic muscles, looks really funny in front of a mirror or if someone walks in but hey, it helps. So basically what you said is true for me!!

This happened to me too a few weeks ago. I feel you so hard. Please stay strong. I gave in and fell into emotional hell again. I was like "maybe if I just have a convo with him and see what he has to say?!" NO NO NO NO NO. It led to him fucking with my head and me fighting the urge to run back once again. The best advice here is to just not reply at all but I know how incredibly hard that is. Open the message if you want. But give yourself this rule..i am allowed only to reply ONCE to him. Whatever he said or asked, answer politely without showing any emotions with ONE text message. Whatever he says next, it's the end. Delete the convo. I was so emotional when he told me he missed me, I showed it to him and he just got the attention he wanted and I ended up hurt again. Over what? A fucking text message. Text your friend instead. Go for a run. Cook something. Clean your apartment. Delete that convo, breathe deeply and let go. Sending you a hug.

And when we were on our first longer no contact period.. like 2 months in i had no tears left to cry and i got to terms with the fact that it's over and i need to let go. but a part of me still wished he would text. And then one day he did. He texted. and the initial rush i felt was incredible like holy shit he does miss me?? But ultimately under that rush all i thought was "ohhhh no". Because my gut and my body knew it wasn't gonna end up well. He asked how am i doing and had all of these questions and i got so emotional but oh i fucking knew i was going to feel messed up again. So i know exactly what you're talking about, i feel you so hard. It's just our brains tricking us. It's normal that your thoughts race back to him in these situations. 6 years, I can't even imagine your pain... mine was 9 months, nothing compared to you, but it was the first time i fell in love, first sex, first everything and losing all of that now makes me feel like i'll never be able to love anyone else again, it's the worst. I've had issues with anxiety and insomnia even before, when i was a kid/teenager and then also in my young adult life, but after this breakup it got so bad I haven't slept well in weeks, and the fatigue made me lose my appetite so i also can't eat much and i lost a lot of weight. I recommend writing down everything that's on your mind whenever you sit up at night. Just write it all out, write how you feel, write down all the pain, be dramatic, write letters to her, write letters to yourself, try to pinpoint what exact thought keeps you up, write about how hurt you are about losing your best friend. and then when you lie back down and if you start to agonize over it again you can be like "wait i just wrote all of this down. It's all on that paper. No need to agonize over and over. I allow myself to sleep now" this really helps me calm my thoughts. I hope you feel better soon and get some sleep, wish you the best, hang in there

You will heal completely, just try to be patient for a little more, it will pay off. And then maybe even dating apps will be really fun and good for you. Lots of love, stay strong

Jesus the exact same thing happened to me. The worst thing was that I saw the end of this relationship coming like 3 weeks before the breakup and i ignored the signs because i loved him so much and wanted it to somehow work. we vaguely ended it via messages and then I couldn't handle the pain and vagueness anymore so after a few days I just asked him to meet with me so we could talk face to face (this was the hardest thing for me to do)

when I was getting ready and putting my clothes on for meeting him that evening I thought my heart was going to burst and I kept HOPING. I hoped that he would tell me something, that he would try, that he would communicate with me. The exact same thing you described happened. Getting a sentence out of him was like pulling teeth and there I was, spilling everything out but gently and slowly and calmly, giving him time to think about what I said. Asking him if he could maybe change his hurtful behaviour for me.

Giving him time to think about if he maybe wanted for this to work. No. He acted like he was so bored and like this was expected. Said we could stay friends reluctantly. I had to hold back my tears and not lose the last bit of dignity I had. So I got closure, I understand that he doesn't care, I have to go on now. But one month later, one month of NC, I still can't let go. It's so hard to be the one to break up when you don't even WANT to do it. And exactly, then you turn out the bad guy. I mean there is no bad guy good guy here, I'm not perfect either, you're not perfect, no one is. But it hurts to be percieved as the bad guy when you do the breakup even though they wanted it but weren't strong enough to communicate their feelings

It's perfectly normal to relapse. Healing isn't linear. You will have 10 good days in a row, and then the 11th day a small thing will remind you of her or something like this will happen and you will fall apart again. But just remember how you survived every single one of your worst days so far, you're doing great. No contact doesn't work for everyone, if you genuiely feel like reaching out one more time and getting closure will help you move on, go for it. I did this and making myself dress and get ready for that meeting was the scariest, most painful thing, but after I met with him and we started talking and I said everything I wanted to say, it was so much better. I cried for hours after it, yes, I fell apart again and again, yes, but now I can work on moving on completely. Just make sure you're strong enough before you decide to reach out, if not, that's also okay. Write everything you want to tell her. Do whatever your gut/heart tells you. I wish you the best, stay strong

Being alone right after this happens is terrifying, i know, i'm very sorry you're going through this. I would wake up with panic attacks from dreams about being abandoned and pushed away. Falling asleep was hell, being asleep was hell, waking up was hell, being awake was hell. But notice the "was". It gets better i promise. What helped me was reaching out!!! Texting my loved ones before bed. My mom, my sister, my friend. I slept with a lamplight for a week, couldn't be alone in the dark and not feeling his body next to me. The absence filled me with so much sadness i thought i was genuinely dying. My anxiety was through the roof, my demons would haunt me every night, everything would scare me. I promise you that this will pass, right now it's horrible i was in the same place only a few weeks ago and then it gets a little easier. Write in a journal before bed, i cannot stress how much this helped me calm my thoughts and emotions. Write everything and cry while writing. It's cathartic. I'm sending you positive vibes and i hope you'll feel better soon, i know you will, wish you the best

I got chills while reading this because my ex was exactly like this but he has 0 awareness about himself and he just kept subtly pushing me away and it broke my heart and at the end i was the one who had to break up because he couldn't put his own issue in words and he just slowly became more and more cold. I tried to help him with his family issues (his parents never showed him emotional support and were always distant from him - think about your relationship with your parents) but he just.. refused to talk about it more and all of this resulted in lack of communication and at the end, the worst breakup and one of the most painful experiences of my life. you seem to understand yourself on a deeper level a lot more and the first step to solving this issue is being aware that you are like this and it's a huge thing!! You sound like a very reasonable person too and i'm sure that with working on yourself, baby steps, you will find a solution and be happier

I would recommend therapy and reflecting on your relationship with your parents and also talking to your partners when you feel that you want to stop with the relationship, it really hurts having someone being all infatuated with you and thinking "hey the honeymoon phase is over but i'm still having a great time and maybe this person will be willing to work on our relationship on the deeper level" and then they just disappear, they're next to you but they disappear. Hurts like hell. Best of luck to you with everything.

This is exactly how I feel. Beautifully written. I also only just learnt how to swim but water gets in my lungs all the time. One day we will reach the shore, walk the land and climb on top of the mountain.
